overview: The Medford City Council and Community Development Board held a joint public hearing to review proposed zoning changes for the Boston Avenue Neighborhood Corridor, focusing on three new sub-districts (BA1, BA2, and BA3). No final vote was taken, and the hearing was continued to June 11th to allow for further refinement of the height limits and use tables.

items.title: Presentation of Proposed Boston Avenue Zoning Districts
items.summary: Consultants presented a plan to create three mixed-use sub-districts with base heights ranging from three to six stories, featuring incentive bonuses for additional height and new standards for drive-through pharmacies. The presentation included shadow studies and an analysis of non-conforming properties to justify the new dimensional standards.

items.title: Council and Board Discussion of Zoning Standards
items.summary: The boards debated the proposed sub-district boundaries and dimensional standards, with Community Development Board Chair Doug Carr proposing significant height reductions in the BA2 and BA3 districts to protect neighborhood character. Members discussed removing parking mandates for lodgers, regulating 'purpose-built student housing,' and requiring special permits for medical offices and doggy daycares.

items.title: Public Comment
items.summary: Residents expressed strong opposition to 10-story buildings and private student housing, citing negative experiences with existing Tufts University structures and concerns over traffic congestion. Other commenters advocated for wider 12-foot sidewalks, increased green space, and higher density to support the Green Line extension.

items.title: Continuance and Direction to Staff
items.summary: The Council and Board voted to continue the joint public hearing to June 11th. The bodies directed city staff and consultants to compile a list of specific proposed amendments, including height limit changes and use table modifications, for evaluation at the next meeting.
